title: ChronicleKinds
description: Which core events become chronicle entries and how their base line reads (B8 R9/R10, D471 D8): the core logs events language-neutrally; the base line is a text key with parameters (DE/EN, no AI). New kinds are data, not code.

event.description: Kind of the core event (WorldEvent.kind) that makes the entry.

text_key.description: Text key of the base line; placeholders are the parameter names in braces.

params.description: Parameters of the base line, used as {placeholders} in the text.

ChronicleParam.description: inhabitant = who (name or neutral number), target = the thing (its name), action = the action or process (vocabulary text), other = a second inhabitant (the event target, by name). A pattern, not an enum: generated C# cannot read arrays of enums.

ChronicleNarrativeSettings.description: B8 R10 (A1355): the day's narrative (family book) in the computing night. At nightfall the core sends the chronicle entries since the last nightfall as one job of kind chronicle; the answer (content guard, length) stands above the day's base lines. Left out = no narrative is asked for.

max_chars.description: Longest narrative in characters (at most the 280 of a generated text).

max_entries.description: At most this many entries go into one job (the newest when there are more).

job_priority.description: Priority of the job (higher runs first).
